title: The Decoy Effect: Does a Worse Option Sway a Model's Choice?

humanBaseline.source: Huber, Payne & Puto (1982), Tables 2 and 3. Across six product categories the no-decoy target share averaged ~0.50; adding an asymmetrically dominated decoy raised it by ~9 points between-subjects (range strategies R/R* ~+13, range-frequency RF ~+8, frequency F ~+4), while the decoy itself was chosen ~1-2% of the time. Per-category target shares are reproduced in the post tables. No per-variant chart overlay (30 conditions would render unreadably); the human comparison lives in the publication's tables.
